For each tower, how do annual mean air temperature and annual precipitation compare with its WorldClim 1970–2000 normal?

E1. Question and hypothesis

Question. For each tower, how do annual mean air temperature and annual precipitation compare with its WorldClim 1970–2000 normal?

Hypothesis. I expect annual temperatures to be mostly above the 1970–2000 normal. I expect precipitation to vary between towers and years. Recent warming may raise temperatures above the older normal. Precipitation may change more from year to year and from site to site.

The five towers are in different regions and ecosystems. They are useful for comparing sites, but they do not represent all climates. Their records cover different periods, so the sites are not compared over the same years.

E2. Data

The analysis uses FLUXNET daily data and two Block 5 datasets: WorldClim and ERA5-Land.

ERA5-Land daily means use UTC days. The downloaded ERA5-Land files have no precipitation values, so I use FLUXNET for precipitation.

Table Table 1 describes the two gridded datasets at each tower and the available FLUXNET record. A blank ERA5-Land period means that the file had no valid daily 2 m temperature values for that tower.

Each tower has its own WorldClim normals. The WorldClim file contains all five towers. ERA5-Land has complete daily data for its available periods at AU-TTE, BE-Bra, CH-Oe1, and US-MN2. The JP-Ynf file has 3,652 dates, but all t2m_C values are missing. I leave them missing and do not fill them from another dataset or tower.

E3. Methods

Download and extraction. WorldClim BIO1 and BIO12 were sampled from the nearest 5′ grid cells using the tower coordinates in EPSG:4326. ERA5-Land daily data were requested from the nearest 0.1° grid cell for the last 10 available years, using coordinates rounded to three decimal places. The analysis settings were unchanged, and the only local script edit replaced the example CDS-key text with a placeholder.

Flux preparation and quality control. I read the daily FLUXMET_DD files from the five original ZIP files and treated -9999 as missing. Annual air temperature is the mean of daily TA_F (°C). Annual precipitation is the sum of daily P_F (mm). For each year, I calculated the mean daily TA_F_QC and P_F_QC values. The merge script does not include these QC columns, so I read them from the original daily files. The data contain 25,202 tower-days and 69 complete site-years. There are no missing TA_F or P_F values.

The first calculation uses all years, regardless of QC. The second keeps years with a mean annual QC fraction of at least 0.90. This cutoff is my choice, not an official FLUXNET pass/fail rule. QC fractions describe the quality of gap-filled data. A year that passes the cutoff can still include gap-filled data. I apply the cutoff separately to temperature and precipitation.

Alignment and analysis. I joined annual FLUXNET values to the WorldClim BIO1 and BIO12 values for each tower, using site_id and year. Temperature departure is annual mean TA_F − BIO1. Precipitation departure is annual sum P_F − BIO12. Positive values mean warmer or wetter conditions than that tower’s normal. I averaged ERA5-Land daily t2m_C by calendar year (UTC) and compared it with BIO1. Missing values stayed as NA.

The pooled median gives each site-year equal weight. Towers with longer records therefore have more influence. Annual values from one tower may not be independent of each other.

E4. Results

The temperature figure compares annual FLUXNET and ERA5-Land departures from each tower’s WorldClim normal. The precipitation figure shows FLUXNET departures from WorldClim BIO12. The zero line means the value equals the WorldClim normal. FLUXNET years below the 0.90 QC cutoff are shown with transparent points and dashed lines. All years remain visible.

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(14, 8), sharey=True, constrained_layout=True)
for ax, site_id in zip(axes.flat, SITE_IDS):
    site = annual[annual["site_id"] == site_id].sort_values("year")
    for i in range(len(site) - 1):
        first = site.iloc[i]
        second = site.iloc[i + 1]
        low_qc = (
            first["ta_qc_fraction"] < QC_THRESHOLD
            or second["ta_qc_fraction"] < QC_THRESHOLD
        )
        ax.plot(
            [first["year"], second["year"]],
            [first["temp_anomaly_C"], second["temp_anomaly_C"]],
            color=site_colors[site_id],
            linewidth=1.35,
            linestyle="--" if low_qc else "-",
            alpha=0.5 if low_qc else 1,
            zorder=2,
        )
    good = site[site["ta_qc_fraction"] >= QC_THRESHOLD]
    low = site[site["ta_qc_fraction"] < QC_THRESHOLD]
    ax.scatter(
        good["year"], good["temp_anomaly_C"], color=site_colors[site_id],
        edgecolor=site_colors[site_id], s=38, zorder=4
    )
    ax.scatter(
        low["year"], low["temp_anomaly_C"], color=site_colors[site_id],
        edgecolor=site_colors[site_id], alpha=0.5, s=38, zorder=4
    )
    era = site.dropna(subset=["era5_anomaly_C"])
    if not era.empty:
        ax.plot(
            era["year"], era["era5_anomaly_C"], color="0.25",
            linestyle=":", linewidth=1.4, marker="D", markersize=4.5, zorder=3
        )
    else:
        ax.text(
            0.5, 0.53, "ERA5-Land unavailable", transform=ax.transAxes,
            ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9
        )
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.9, linestyle="--", zorder=1)
    ax.set_title(site_id)
    ax.set_xlabel("Year")
    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)

legend_ax = axes.flat[5]
legend_ax.axis("off")
legend_ax.legend(

The table shows medians and means of annual departures. It includes all years and a second calculation with annual QC ≥ 0.90.

Code 
summary_rows = []
for variable, value_col, qc_col in [
    ("Temperature (°C)", "temp_anomaly_C", "ta_qc_fraction"),
    ("Precipitation (mm/year)", "precip_anomaly_mm", "precip_qc_fraction"),
]:
    for label, subset in [
        ("No QC filter", annual),
        ("Annual QC ≥ 0.90", annual[annual[qc_col] >= QC_THRESHOLD]),
    ]:
        valid = subset.dropna(subset=[value_col])
        summary_rows.append(
            {
                "Variable": variable,
                "Version": label,
                "Site-years (n)": len(valid),
                "Towers (n)": valid["site_id"].nunique(),
                "Pooled mean": valid[value_col].mean(),
                "Pooled median": valid[value_col].median(),
            }
        )
summary_table = pd.DataFrame(summary_rows)
summary_table.round(2)
Annual climate departures from WorldClim, with unfiltered and QC ≥ 0.90 summaries.
Variable Version Site-years (n) Towers (n) Pooled mean Pooled median
0 Temperature (°C) No QC filter 69 5 0.48 0.50
1 Temperature (°C) Annual QC ≥ 0.90 54 5 0.62 0.64
2 Precipitation (mm/year) No QC filter 69 5 736.65 34.91
3 Precipitation (mm/year) Annual QC ≥ 0.90 47 4 -17.47 -8.92

Without QC filtering, the median departure is +0.50 °C for temperature (69 site-years, five towers) and +34.91 mm/year for precipitation (69 site-years, five towers). With annual QC ≥ 0.90, the medians are +0.64 °C (54 site-years, five towers) and −8.93 mm/year (47 site-years, four towers). These results describe the available site-years. They are not estimates of a global climate trend.

The unfiltered means are +0.48 °C and +736.65 mm/year. The high precipitation mean is mainly caused by the unreliable JP-Ynf precipitation data. At JP-Ynf, P_F_QC is zero in all ten years, so no years from this site pass the precipitation QC cutoff. I include the unfiltered result for comparison, but it should not be treated as reliable.

As a second temperature check, the median of the four tower means for ERA5-Land is +1.04 °C (38 site-years). JP-Ynf has no valid ERA5-Land data. The other four tower means are above their WorldClim normals. ERA5-Land does not provide precipitation data for this analysis.

E5. Discussion

The temperature results support the hypothesis at most towers. The QC-filtered median is above the WorldClim normal, and all four towers with ERA5-Land data also have positive mean departures. Not every year is warmer than normal. Most annual temperature departures at JP-Ynf are below its normal. Precipitation departures differ among towers and years. The unfiltered result is affected by JP-Ynf, where precipitation QC is zero. WorldClim and ERA5-Land grid cells are about 9 km wide. This is much larger than the approximate 100 m–1 km tower footprint, so grid values may not match the conditions near a tower. WorldClim describes 1970–2000, while tower records cover different years from 1999 to 2025. These results show differences from an older normal, not a trend based on the same years. The main limits are missing ERA5-Land temperature for JP-Ynf, poor precipitation QC there, the chosen 0.90 cutoff, and the small number of towers. Values from different years at one tower may not be independent.
